text:
alex: Quick q — trying to settle span naming + attrs for LLM inference traces. I'm leaning toward a stable span.name that describes the operation, not the model id. e.g. 'inference.request' or 'llm.generate'. Thoughts?

mira: +1 for stable name. Putting model details as attributes seems cleaner for querying. span.name should be what happened, not who did it.

sam: We also need to think about routing/exports. If span.name has model, we'll explode cardinality and make index retention a mess.

jordan: Agree re cardinality. Proposal: span.name = 'llm.request' with attribute model.name and model.revision (or variant). Also add operation attribute like op=generate|embed|rerank.

alex: That sounds good. What about token counts and cache hits? We need those in telemetry for cost and cache efficiency dashboards.

mira: Put token counts and cache as attributes: "llm.input_tokens", "llm.output_tokens", "kvcache.hit" (boolean) and maybe "kvcache.items_returned". Keep them as attributes not in name.

sam: Also recommend normalized attr keys: prefix with "llm." or "model." to avoid key collisions. Example set:
```
span.name = "llm.request"
attributes = {
  "llm.op": "generate",
  "model.name": "gpt-large-v2",
  "model.variant": "qy8-q4",
  "llm.input_tokens": 48,
  "llm.output_tokens": 152,
  "llm.cost_usd_est": 0.0032,
  "kvcache.hit": true
}
```

jordan: One caveat: some exporters (older logging backends) struggle with lots of numeric attributes per-span. We need a retention/export policy: sample full spans with heavy attrs, and send a thin version for bulk export.

alex: Right — suggested export strategy: always export full attrs for errors and high-latency traces; otherwise export a minimal attr set: llm.op, model.name, llm.output_tokens. Full enrich on sampled traces. Could we use a two-tier span: root span minimal and a child span with enrichment sampled?

mira: That could work if the runtime supports adding child span post-hoc before export. Another approach: attach heavy_metrics as a single serialized JSON attr when sampling isn't on, e.g. "llm.metrics_blob" but that hurts queryability.

sam: For dashboards we want numeric tokens to be native numeric fields for aggregation. So prefer exporting them as top-level numeric attrs on sampled spans and in aggregated metrics pipeline (OTLP -> metrics).

jordan: Ops note: we should include a fixed enum for op to avoid freeform strings. ops values: generate, embed, rerank, summarize, chat. Helps with retention/rollup.

alex: Good call. Also propose standardizing span.name pattern for cross-service joins: use service-prefix like "runtime.llm.request" vs just "llm.request"? Any preference?

mira: I prefer keeping span.name short to avoid duplication; use service.name tag on resource to disambiguate. So "llm.request" + resource.service = runtime/dedicated/hosted.

sam: One more implementation detail: ensure token counts are recorded before any truncation/hard-limits. We need both input_tokens_received and input_tokens_sent_to_model after truncation. Maybe: "llm.input_tokens_raw" and "llm.input_tokens_used".

jordan: +1, helpful for debugging cost/regressions.

alex: Okay action items:
- adopt span.name = "llm.request"
- attributes: normalized keys under "llm." and "model." including op enum, model.name, model.variant, llm.input_tokens_raw, llm.input_tokens_used, llm.output_tokens, kvcache.hit
- sampling/export policy: always-full for errors/latency>threshold, 1% baseline sample for successful requests, and configurable on a per-customer basis for Dedicated/Private
- add a follow-up RFC for exporter behavior (OTLP vs logs) and a small shim that can emit a minimal metric for every request (tokens/cost) even when span sampling is low

mira: I'll draft the RFC and include a couple of example queries for dashboards (e.g., pct cache hit by model, cost per op per model).

telemetry-bot: Note: new span attr naming conventions saved to /infra/telemetry/llm_span_naming.md (draft).

alex: Thanks — let's review RFC in eng-runtime sync next Wed. :thumbsup:
